slides.title: AI Updates Users are Upset about Gemini 3.5
slides.text: AI Updates Users are Upset about Gemini 3.5 Flash https://x.com/jeremyphoward/status/2057923197639840033 It's intelligence and speed is awesome. Absolutely amazing. It's incredible for example with RLM type tasks, full autonomy, swarms with critics. But it's been trained to max evals. It goes off and does random crap It's not very useful in cooperative/iterative settings, where I want it to work with me, not for me. I want to interactively experiment. I don't want it to go off and decide to do everything for me. I want to work iteratively. My work always involves me building a deeper understanding of the problem space I'm working in through iterative development and experimentation Model tries to be "smart" about what you want instead of just executing the task; super frustrating when you need predictable outputs for production stuff. feels like they optimized for demo wow factor over actual usefulness I think this is the natural consequence of evals that reward 'helpfulness' through proxy metrics. The model learned that doing extra stuff correlates with higher scores, so it generalizes that pattern everywhere. Annoying as hell but makes perfect sense

slides.title: MCP Tunnels MCP Tunnels (Anthropic in May 2026)
slides.text: MCP Tunnels MCP Tunnels (Anthropic in May 2026) a part of claude managed agents release Claude Managed Agents run on Anthropic infrastructure Suppose you have a local MCP server. How external managed agents can access internal MCP server? Instead of opening inbound firewall ports, organization can establish a single outbound, encrypted mTLS connection to Anthropic's infrastructure. This way the credentials stay inside. The external managed agent never handles auth tokens Both Anthropic and OpenAI now offer this capability. The feature is currently in research preview # server.py from fastmcp import FastMCP mcp = FastMCP("echo-server") @mcp.tool() def hello(name: str) -> str: return f"Hello, {name}!" if __name__ == "__main__": mcp.run(transport="streamable-http", port=8000) import anthropic client = anthropic.Anthropic() response = client.beta.messages.create( model="claude-opus-4-7", max_tokens=1000, messages=[{ "role": "user", "content": "Use the hello tool to greet tunnel." }], mcp_servers=[{ "type": "url", "url": " https://echo.YOUR_TUNNEL_DOMAIN_HERE/mcp ", "name": "echo", }], tools=[{"type": "mcp_toolset", "mcp_server_name": "echo"}], betas=["mcp-client-2025-11-20"], ) print(response) The code on the right shows simple example The server.py runs inside your private network on port 8000 cloudflared (the tunnel agent) creates an outbound-only encrypted connection to Anthropic's edge, exposing your server at echo.YOUR_TUNNEL_DOMAIN_HERE The Messages API call passes that tunnel URL in mcp_servers, and Claude invokes your hello tool over the tunnel You create your tunnel and get your YOUR_TUNNEL_DOMAIN_HERE value from the Claude Console > MCP Tunnels section. # Install cloudflared on macOS brew install cloudflared # Start a quick tunnel pointing at your local MCP server cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:8000

slides.title: Harness engineering - a system around the model
slides.text: Harness engineering - a system around the model Tools, constraints, feedback loops, and interfaces Instead of obsessing over the perfect prompt, focus on how the agent operates over time: what it’s allowed to do, how it checks its work, and how failures are caught and corrected https://github.com/walkinglabs/learn-harness-engineering A practical harness usually includes: clear task specs and guides; a tool layer (files, VCS, linters, CI, external APIs); state and memory (task lists, scratchpads, logs); evaluation (tests, secondary model, or human-in-the-loop); safety/guardrails (permissions, rate limits, rollback paths) Start small: wrap one concrete workflow with scripted setup, deterministic checkpoints, and automated verification before and after each agent action Each time the agent fails, don’t just tweak the prompt: add or refine a harness rule, tool, or check so that specific failure becomes less likely in the future https://www.reddit.com/r/ClaudeAI/comments/1s9jm0d/i_had_claude_read_every_harness_engineering_guide/ AI Updates

slides.title: How to make an agent with zero Hallucinations
slides.text: How to make an agent with zero Hallucinations xxx Agent with Zero Hallucinations Hermes Agent Runs Codex and Claude In One Agent Nemanja Mirkovic demonstrates a collaborative AI workflow by combining three top tools: Hermes Agent, Codex, and Claude https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O-PEeD7fymo ECC (Everything Claude Code) - open-source meta-harness Built on top of Anthropic's Claude Code coding agent It extends Claude Code with structured skills, reusable workflows, custom slash commands, memory, and security patterns to make AI coding agents significantly more effective. The repository has earned over 182K GitHub stars and 28K forks. ECC 2.0 aims to become a universal harness compatible with other AI coding tools like Cursor and Codex, not just Claude Code. A companion tool called AgentShield scans agent configs and MCP servers for security vulnerabilities. A hosted version is available at ecc.tools starting at $19/month. https://github.com/affaan-m/ECC - 192K stars

slides.title: Why Google invested $40B in Anthropic April 7
slides.text: Why Google invested $40B in Anthropic April 7 - Anthropic ARR $1B to $9B in just one year April 20 - Amazon wires Anthropic $5B with a $20B option on top, locking in a $100B AWS infrastructure commitment over 10 years April 23 - OpenAI releases internal "GPT 5.5" (code-named Spud) April 24 - Google panics and wires $10 Bln to Anthropic (with an agreement pledging up to $30 Bln more in milestone payments) China's DeepSeek drops its V4 model running on Huawei chips for pennies, completely bypassing Nvidia hardware Google's staggering $40 billion investment in Anthropic marks a fundamental shift in the AI race, moving from simple chatbots to autonomous enterprise agents and massive infrastructure capture Google was heavily pressured by the explosive rise of Claude Code, which dominates 54% of the enterprise AI coding market and runs workflows autonomously for over 30 hours. Furthermore, Anthropic’s secret Mythos model shocked the industry by scoring 83.1% on cybersecurity benchmarks, proving capable of independently fixing decades-old infrastructure vulnerabilities Ultimately, this deal is a proxy war over compute: Google and Amazon are leveraging Anthropic’s massive workloads on their custom TPU and Trainium chips to aggressively break Nvidia's hardware monopoly ahead of Anthropic's projected $950 billion IPO AI Updates Anthropic closing $30 Bln funding at $900 Bln Valuation This is the largest private AI fundraise in history. Compare: Nvidia $5.2T, Alphabet (Google) $4.8T, Apple $4.3T, Microsoft $3.1T, Meta $1.55T, SpaceX (targeting IPO) $1.5T, OpenAI $0.85T

slides.title: Claude Managed Agents on Cloudflare Cloudflare and Anthropic
slides.text: Claude Managed Agents on Cloudflare Cloudflare and Anthropic have partnered Claude Managed Agents is a hosted service on the Anthropic platform that lets developers define and run long-horizon AI agents capable of reading files, executing code, running commands, and browsing the web The integration uses Cloudflare's global network to provide secure, isolated sandboxes for each agent session, private connectivity to internal services, and custom tool support via Cloudflare bindings like R2, D1, and KV Anthropic describes the architecture as decoupling the "brain" (the agent loop running on Anthropic) from the "hands," the execution environment running on Cloudflare https://blog.cloudflare.com/claude-managed-agents/ AI Updates "Compassion – that’s the one thing no machine ever had. Maybe it’s the one thing that keeps man ahead of them." - Dr. McCoy

slides.title: Google AI Co-Scientist Google published its AI Co-Scientist
slides.text: Google AI Co-Scientist Google published its AI Co-Scientist research in Nature Introducing Hypothesis Generation - a Gemini-powered tool that uses competing AI agents in "idea tournaments" to generate and rank scientific hypotheses Inspired by AlphaGo, agents propose, critique, and refine ideas collaboratively In one Stanford test, a Co-Scientist drug lead reduced a liver-fibrosis scarring signal by 91% Google also launched Gemini for Science, bundling Co-Scientist with AlphaEvolve and NotebookLM into a unified research toolkit https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-026-10644-y AI Updates AutoResearchClaw: Self-Reinforcing Autonomous Research with Human-AI Collaboration Open-source framework (Google, Stanford, UC Berkeley, Mea, Carnegie Mellon) AutoResearchClaw code is hosted on GitHub, uses OpenClaw and Claw4Science Competitors - Sakana AI's The Scientist and Aris https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.20025

slides.title: AI Updates OpenAI Model solves 80y old math
slides.text: AI Updates OpenAI Model solves 80y old math problem An new unreleased OpenAI reasoning model disproved a 1946 conjecture by mathematician Paul Erdős about planar unit distances This problem had stood unsolved for nearly 80 years Top mathematicians verified the result as genuinely novel and publishable The breakthrough came by connecting discrete geometry with algebraic number theory, two fields rarely bridged Experts say the AI didn't use exotic math, but excelled at cross-disciplinary synthesis — finding a path that human specialists could have discovered had they collaborated across fields. https://openai.com/index/model-disproves-discrete-geometry-conjecture/ https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.20695v1 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Br4l9YjCyRU - video featuring Fields Medalist Timothy Gowers and the team DeepSeek "Thinking-with-Visual-Primitives" paper https://github.com/ailuntx/Thinking-with-Visual-Primitives Instead of describing images using text, this method allows AI to think with visual primitives The AI can seamlessly handle tasks like counting and topological reasoning Incredibly, this system uses 90% fewer visual tokens than top commercial models, making it faster and cheaper to run while matching or beating frontier models across seven external benchmarks http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LpXhy2iiaQE - video

slides.title: OpenSpec spec-driven development OpenSpec is an open-source, spec-driven
slides.text: OpenSpec spec-driven development OpenSpec is an open-source, spec-driven development framework for AI coding assistants like Claude Code and Cursor OpenSpec solves a core problem of preserving the intent and requirements It solves the core problem with AI-assisted coding: intent and requirements get lost across scattered chat sessions, leading to unpredictable results OpenSpec fixes this by storing structured specification files directly in your repository, giving both developers and AI agents a shared, persistent source of truth before any code is written. It uses two folders - one for current specs and one for proposed changes It uses a simple CLI workflow to create proposals, implement them, and archive completed work Everything is plain Markdown, checked into Git, with no API keys or external services required https://openspec.dev - https://openspec.pro - https://github.com/Fission-AI/OpenSpec - https://github.com/wearetechnative/awesome-openspec AI Updates HASP (Harnessing LLM Agents with Skill Programs) Paper by NYU and Salesforce AI - https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.17734 HASP wraps a base LLM in an external Python control harness It converts passive textual skills into executable Program Functions (PFs) that act as strict, deterministic guardrails. Operating like physics' Maxwell's demon , the harness monitors the agent's state When a failure-prone state is detected, the harness actively intercepts it - either overriding the action or injecting corrective context Tests show this inference-time loop intervention dramatically boosts accuracy from 31.2% to 51% . https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M7imuqrQ6bY

slides.title: Quantum-informed AI for Chaotic Processes "Quantum-informed machine learning
slides.text: Quantum-informed AI for Chaotic Processes "Quantum-informed machine learning for predicting spatiotemporal chaos with practical quantum advantage" A team at University College London has achieved a major breakthrough by training AI using data processed by a quantum computer This "quantum-informed" AI can predict highly chaotic and complex systems - such as weather, turbulence, and disease spread - with roughly 20% greater accuracy than classical AI , while requiring far less memory Unlike regular models that lose accuracy over time, this system uncovers stable, hidden patterns within apparent randomness This technology will revolutionize climate science, medicine, and energy grid management https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13089341/ https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ikj7f1MSUeo - video AI Updates Top View Agent V2 with Seedance 2.0 model from ByteDance Generate quick, cohesive, long-form videos https://www.topview.ai - monthly subscriptions ($0,$16,$44,$50) Top View Agent V2 collapses five distinct tools (scripts, voices, images, clips, and editing) into a single conversational interface Users chat with the AI agent to co-create a structured storyboard This allows creators to adjust visual styles and scenes before generation, resulting in quick, cohesive, long-form videos with an integrated timeline editor for final touches https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M5xTskx4SUY - video

slides.title: Multiverse Computing - LLM + quantum blocks Meta's
slides.text: Multiverse Computing - LLM + quantum blocks Meta's Llama 3.1 8B model + a small set of quantum circuit blocks (6K params) Running this hybrid system on IBM's 156-qubit quantum processor Reduced the model's perplexity by 1.4% The improvement may sound modest, but it had meaningful real-world effects: the quantum-enhanced model correctly answered astronomy and biology questions that the original Llama model got wrong The team argues this result proves quantum computing can meaningfully improve AI reasoning, with gains expected to grow as quantum hardware matures https://www.livescience.com/technology/quantum/scientists-trained-an-ai-model-using-an-ibm-quantum-computer-and-it-answered-questions-correctly-that-the-base-model-couldnt AI Updates AI Will Deliver Wisdom Wisdom is a probabilistic pattern recognition across vast human experience FutureSim - a new benchmark replays real-world events and asks AI to forecast 90 days ahead It shows that frontier models like GPT 5.5 already outperforming crowd prediction markets AI can simulate billions of interventions to identify optimal outcomes in medicine, economics, and geopolitics This "artificial wisdom" may matter more than AGI, since intelligence solves problems while wisdom chooses "which" problems to solve Peter Diamandis calls on leaders in business and government to embed predictive AI into decision-making before major choices are made https://metatrends.substack.com/p/ai-will-deliver-wisdom

slides.title: Quantum is Breaking Encryption https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.28846 "Securing Elliptic Curve
slides.text: Quantum is Breaking Encryption https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.28846 "Securing Elliptic Curve Cryptocurrencies against Quantum Vulnerabilities: Resource Estimates and Mitigations" The team of Google researches demonstrated that Shor's algorithm can break the 256-bit Elliptic Curve Discrete Logarithm Problem (the backbone of Bitcoin and most blockchain cryptography) using fewer than 1,200 logical qubits and 90 million Toffoli gates On superconducting architectures with current error rates, this could execute in minutes using fewer than half a million physical qubits The paper distinguishes between fast-clock (superconducting, photonic) and slow-clock (neutral atom, ion trap) architectures and their different threat profiles It urges all vulnerable cryptocurrency communities to migrate to Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) without delay https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=H_fQXu9vigk - video AI Updates

slides.title: Obsidian stores data as a directory tree of
slides.text: Obsidian stores data as a directory tree of markdown files ( called "vault" ) plus a small amount of app metadata; it is basically a personal wiki with some indexing Each note is a plain ".md" file . You can mix in images, PDFs, and other arbitrary files in the same tree Obsidian adds a ".obsidian" folder at the root of the vault for app config (plugins, appearance, hotkeys, workspace state, etc.); deleting it does not delete any notes No database, no proprietary format, and you can still use grep, rg, etc directly over the vault if you want Obsidian uses wiki‑style links and builds its link graph from that; Internal links are written as `[[Note Title]]` or `[[path/to/note|Display Text]]` . If the target doesn’t exist yet, you can click to create a new note A vault is a folder and subfolders; Many people use folders like `docs/`, `projects/`, `attachments/`, etc. inside the vault When you paste or drag‑and‑drop an image into a note, Obsidian saves it as a file and inserts a markdown image link; You can configure where new attachments go:  Vault root, same folder as the current note, or a specific “attachments” folder or path Obsidian does build some indices for performance and metadata, but these are auxiliary, not your source of truth Obsidian maintains a “metadata cache” in an internal IndexedDB database and cache files, not in your notes themselves Obsidian - for Memory, RAG, MCP Full‑text search in the app uses this metadata cache; from the user’s perspective it’s effectively instant for typical vault sizes If an external agent modifies markdown files, Obsidian rescans and updates its metadata cache The “wiki engine” part (graph, backlinks, search, plugins) is provided by the app, but the content is just text files you already know how to manage You can have multiple vaults (directories) - for example, personal, client1, client2, ... You can use Google Drive to sync folders across devices There are community plugins (e.g. “Obsidian Google Drive” and “OGD Sync”) that sync a local vault to a Drive using Drive’s API Obsidian recommends its own Obsidian Sync service

slides.text: 9 essential AI skills to build wealth - Sabrina Ramonov https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=d81xtxGFwHg 1. Ask AI for answers first before using search engines 2. Always verify AI-output to catch potential hallucinations 3. Provide rich context - info, constraints, clarifying examples 4. Use AI for learning before consulting high-cost experts 5. Treat AI like a new hire: Provide continuous feedback over time 6. Allow AI to refine its own work (iterate, grade, improve) 7. Audit and document processes - weekly automation 8. Use AI agents with tools and everyday apps 9. Apply AI to improve and scale working processes Build Business with AI Startup Solo With AI Agents - Ryan Carson Start with docs, rules, skills for agents (create employees) Use "Claw Chief" (cron jobs and md files) to run every 15 min - scheduling, inbox sweeps, push slack messages; The system has its own email address and GitHub account to function exactly like a human employee Every night, the AI does lead generation via Firecrawl, writes details to a CRM Google Sheet, and drafts cold outreach emails Devon on cloud for 100% of his software engineering (coding, PRs, testing, merging) - 10-20 PRs/day autonomously Carson chats to Devon with Google Ads API to manage ad campaigns AI is used to cut expert interviews into short segments via Descript, uploads them to Google Drive, and lets an automated nightly playbook use Gemini to watch the video and generate text copy OpenAI’s image model handles ad and video creative http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IDqdVZwAwjw
